nodes.label: Floating-point non-associativity, thread counts and seeds

ADR-0002: same lock, machine and thread count gave bitwise identical LSTM weights; 1 and 2 threads agreed, 4 differed; torch's default 20 threads ran 6.7-20x slower than 8. Hence tolerances in tests, conclusions checked across seeds, explicit thread count (fixture uses 1).

nodes.label: Diebold-Mariano test (rectangular LRV with HLN factor, Bartlett fallback)
nodes.norm_label: diebold-mariano test (rectangular lrv with hln factor, bartlett fallback)
nodes.rationale: Truncation of the long-run variance at lag h-1 is an assumption; under a state-dependent null the ADR measured size 0.1258 at n=583 (open item O6, decided in M5). Rectangular weights are used because Bartlett at lag h-1 under-estimates the LRV of MA(h-1) differentials; statsmodels diebold_mariano_test uses Bartlett and is not used.

nodes.label: Mincer-Zarnowitz regression and joint Wald test
nodes.norm_label: mincer-zarnowitz regression and joint wald test
nodes.rationale: a=0 alone is not unbiasedness; the joint test of (a,b)=(0,1) tests both unbiasedness and efficiency. The Wald test uses Newey-West at lag h-1 with the same Bartlett bias (open item O5).

nodes.label: Assumptions and where it breaks (structural breaks, vintage, cost of purging)
nodes.norm_label: assumptions and where it breaks (structural breaks, vintage, cost of purging)

nodes.label: Look-ahead rules L1-L7
nodes.rationale: L1 trailing windows only (no centered rolling, no bfill); L2 label availability; L3 scalers fitted per cutoff on update rows only; L4 early-stopping block with an h-session purge; L5 fixed regime thresholds; L6 hyper-parameters chosen on dev only; L7 trade at the close of t+1 (VIX close may be struck at 16:15 ET after VXX's 16:00 close, to verify in M1).

nodes.label: Overlapping h-step errors are MA(h-1), so DM needs HAC
nodes.norm_label: overlapping h-step errors are ma(h-1), so dm needs hac
nodes.rationale: For a random walk the h-step errors have autocorrelation (h-k)/h (0.9524 at lag 1 for h=21) and long-run variance h*sigma_e^2, so the i.i.d. standard error is too small by sqrt(21)=4.58 and DM would reject far too often.

nodes.label: Rectangular long-run variance with HLN factor and Bartlett fallback
nodes.norm_label: rectangular long-run variance with hln factor and bartlett fallback
nodes.rationale: Bartlett weights at lag h-1 give 14.02 sigma_e^2 instead of 21 (standard error 0.817 of truth), whereas equal weights are exact for MA(h-1). ADR-0001 4.8 (as amended) uses rectangular at lag h-1 times the HLN factor with t_{n-1} p-values (0.9648 for n=583, h=21), Bartlett as flagged fallback if the estimate is <= 0; ADR simulation rejection 0.0636 vs 0.1189 at nominal 5%.

nodes.label: Off-the-shelf statsmodels DM uses Bartlett, not this estimator
nodes.norm_label: off-the-shelf statsmodels dm uses bartlett, not this estimator
nodes.rationale: In pinned statsmodels 0.15.0 diebold_mariano_test defaults to lags=max(h-1, ceil(n^(1/3))) with HAC Bartlett weights: t=-1.3318 equals hand-coded Bartlett while rectangular gives -1.0440. M5 must pin the lags and code the rectangular estimator.

nodes.label: Truncation test as a property test
nodes.norm_label: truncation test as a property test
nodes.rationale: For every origin t, the forecast from data up to t must equal the forecast from all data (LSTM within tolerance); a seeded random sample of origins avoids adding hypothesis. It catches centred windows, bfill, full-sample scaling and label leaks but cannot catch leaks identical in both runs (eyeballed thresholds, holdout-tuned hyper-parameters, data restatements). Sketch for M2, not existing code.

nodes.label: Walk-forward protocol: expanding window, 63-session refit, frozen parameters, daily state
nodes.norm_label: walk-forward protocol: expanding window, 63-session refit, frozen parameters, daily state
nodes.rationale: Expanding windows keep rare regimes such as 2008 and 2020 while rolling windows adapt to breaks but forget crises; ADR-0001 4.5 expands for every model. Within a fold parameters are frozen but state (GARCH recursion, HAR regressors, LSTM window) updates daily with data up to t.

nodes.label: Fair model comparison: identical folds, label availability, RMSE and QLIKE primary
nodes.norm_label: fair model comparison: identical folds, label availability, rmse and qlike primary
nodes.rationale: Expanding window refitted every 63 sessions with parameters frozen within a fold; a training example counts only if its target date is on or before the cutoff; DM requires identical origins; MAE favours the median and MAPE lower forecasts so they are reported but flagged.

nodes.label: Risks and mitigations (look-ahead, overlapping horizons, regimes, overfitting)
nodes.norm_label: risks and mitigations (look-ahead, overlapping horizons, regimes, overfitting)
nodes.rationale: Mitigations: shared folds, train-only fitting, dev-only tuning and a truncation test; lag h-1 variance estimator with small-sample correction (may still over-reject under vol clustering, O6); regime breakdown kept local and a fixed holdout start of 2024-07-01 so Aug-2024 and Apr-2025 are inside; DSR counts every variant. Not beating the random walk would still be a valid result.

nodes.label: Success metrics (process pass/fail)
nodes.rationale: Four process checks: one command reproduces every reports/ table from a clean clone; a mutation-checked test fails if forecast origins differ and a truncation test passes for every model; DM tests against the random walk with no empty cells; every README/PR-FAQ number re-measured by verifier with the adversarial ledger committed.

nodes.label: Calendar and folds derived from dates, not data; forecasting separate from scoring
nodes.norm_label: calendar and folds derived from dates, not data; forecasting separate from scoring
nodes.rationale: Cutoffs are anchored backwards from holdout_start, so a truncated run could not derive them; the schedule is a pure function of (calendar, dev_start, holdout_start, fold_len) passed into every run. The evaluable-origin rule only filters scoring, so a run truncated at t still forecasts at t.

nodes.label: DM lag-(h-1) cut-off is an assumption (open item O6)
nodes.norm_label: dm lag-(h-1) cut-off is an assumption (open item o6)
nodes.rationale: Optimal errors are MA(h-1) but d_t need not be under nonlinear losses, and it fails when relative accuracy depends on a persistent vol state. Review B's state-dependent null gave rejection 0.1258 (n=583) and 0.1103 (n=2000) against 0.0563 and 0.0507 for a symmetric control, so p-values can be about 2.5 times too liberal; O6 has M5 pick a remedy by measurement. MZ still uses Newey-West at lag h-1 (O5).

nodes.label: Identical folds for every model (paired comparison)
nodes.norm_label: identical folds for every model (paired comparison)
nodes.rationale: Var(d)=Var(La)+Var(Lb)-2Cov(La,Lb): with sd 10 each and correlation 0.9, sd(d)=4.47 against 14.14 unpaired. Pairing needs identical origins and information, which the DM test needs in M5.

nodes.label: Label-availability rule L2: usable only if tau + h <= cutoff
nodes.norm_label: label-availability rule l2: usable only if tau + h <= cutoff
nodes.rationale: Without the rule the 21 pairs tau=80..100 leak labels up to 21 sessions past a cutoff at 100; for RV21 the pair at tau=100 holds the whole window the first forecast must predict. The rule costs 21 pairs out of thousands.

nodes.label: Scaling: fit scalers on training data only (L3)
nodes.norm_label: scaling: fit scalers on training data only (l3)
nodes.rationale: Worked example: train [12,14,13,15] then a spike; a train-only AR(1) forecasts 14.85 from 15 while a full-sample scaler forecasts 15.65. The 0.8 gap equals (1-phi)(21.5-13.5): reversion to a mean only the future reveals.

nodes.label: Fixed holdout_start 2024-07-01 (open item O1)
nodes.rationale: A trailing 24-month window would start 2024-10-28, miss the 5-Aug-2024 spike, and move at every refresh, sliding seen dates into out-of-sample. The fixed holdout is 583 sessions = 9*63+16 (10 folds, last partial); the first 50 sessions of 2000 are burn-in.

nodes.label: Four failed licensing assumptions
nodes.rationale: A published mean times its n is a sum, and sums subtract. (1) >=20 dates per cell failed on 583->584; (2) refresh by >=20 dates with blank siblings failed as RW bias telescopes; (3) 'losses, not signed contrasts' failed via EDA sd, MZ fit and DM mean_d; (4) 'an SPX-tied row needs SPX' failed because SPX is public (review E recovered holdout mean VIX to median 4.29%, max 13.69%). nodes.rationale: Key order changes bytes and SHA-256 for the same content, so sort_keys=True; NaN is not JSON (Node's JSON.parse throws), so allow_nan=False forces an explicit null; default ensure_ascii keeps bytes independent of platform encoding.

nodes.label: Walkthrough of src/ivf/config.py and src/ivf/contract.py
nodes.rationale: serialise uses allow_nan=False, sort_keys=True and compact separators; _check_json forces str keys because json.dumps sorts int keys before stringifying, giving one JSON value two hashes.

nodes.label: Rounding needs a one-unit --check tolerance
nodes.rationale: If two runs differ by less than one unit q of the last exported decimal, their rounded values differ by at most q (2.675 is stored below and rounds to 2.67 while the next double rounds to 2.68). ADR-0001 D5's one-unit tolerance is sound only if run-to-run noise is far below q.

nodes.norm_label: d3: storage layout (raw, interim, processed, reports, app data)

nodes.norm_label: d5: determinism and reproducibility (pins, seeds, --check, contract tests)
nodes.rationale: Seeds use SeedSequence with stable keys (sha256 of model_id, cutoff date, member) because positional keys reshuffle when models.yaml is reordered and Python hash() is salted per process; the committed fixture uses 1 thread so it reproduces across machines.

nodes.label: Fetch idempotency and provenance chain (sha256 raw files, append-only JSONL)
nodes.norm_label: fetch idempotency and provenance chain (sha256 raw files, append-only jsonl)
nodes.rationale: Content-addressed immutable raw files let any result be rebuilt from exact bytes; append-only JSONL cannot be corrupted by a crash the way a rewritten parquet could.

nodes.label: run_id and protocol_hash identities
nodes.rationale: run_id is 12 hex of a SHA-256 over protocol_hash, source_commit, source_dirty, data_mode and sorted raw hashes, so identical inputs overwrite their own partition; it is provenance and therefore ignored by --check.

nodes.label: arch EGARCH: simulation needs rng= (random_state ignored) and lower-case method
nodes.norm_label: arch egarch: simulation needs rng= (random_state ignored) and lower-case method
nodes.rationale: EGARCH has no analytic forecast beyond 1 step; method='simulation' ignores random_state=, and arch 8.0.0 silently runs the bootstrap for 'Simulation' or 'SIMULATION' because the dispatch compares the raw string. A silently ignored seed is worse than none; test that two forecasts with a fresh seeded rng agree to the last digit.

nodes.norm_label: pmdarima predict requires python int n_periods (np.int64 raises typeerror)

nodes.label: LSTM reproducibility: bitwise identical only on same lock, machine and thread count
nodes.norm_label: lstm reproducibility: bitwise identical only on same lock, machine and thread count
nodes.rationale: Changing thread count changes low-order bits and CPU/GPU final validation MSE differ by about 4e-7, so tests compare LSTM outputs with tolerances and conclusions are checked across seeds rather than by matching hashes across machines.

nodes.norm_label: auto_arima never recovers true ar(2) order (picks (1,0,2)/(1,0,3))

nodes.norm_label: pypi default torch on linux aarch64 is the cuda 13.0 build (3.16 gb)

nodes.norm_label: per-date results count as the data
nodes.rationale: The cumulative sum of a random-walk forecast's errors rebuilds the VIX path, so real per-date forecasts, errors and equity curves are never committed or bundled into dist/.

nodes.norm_label: publication set p: the only real-data numbers that may be committed

P items, all per whole period (dev, holdout): RMSE and QLIKE as ratios to the random walk (3 s.f.), MAE and MAPE likewise flagged not consistent for the mean; DM statistic (HLN) and p-value (2 dp); MZ as pass/fail only; Sharpe, PSR, DSR (2 dp), n_trials exact, turnover (2 s.f.); AR(1) half-life of ln(index) in sessions (2 s.f.); n. nodes.norm_label: what was built in m0 (design, package skeleton, contract, tools, tests, app shell)

nodes.norm_label: d1: python computes, json carries, the app renders
nodes.rationale: A number the app computes is a second implementation nobody tests against the first; with the split a reviewer re-measures every published number in one place (Python) and the app is tested only for drawing the data correctly.

nodes.norm_label: d2: publish a closed set of unitless results, never the series

nodes.label: Per-date errors and equity curves count as the licensed series (telescoping)
nodes.norm_label: per-date errors and equity curves count as the licensed series (telescoping)
nodes.rationale: Random-walk h=1 error e_t = V_{t+1} - V_t, so the cumulative sum rebuilds the VIX path up to a constant; the always-long-VXX equity curve is the VXX price path rescaled. Hence license_class series vs aggregate in the manifest.

nodes.norm_label: tolerant reader (producer validates strictly, app checks major and used fields)
nodes.rationale: Schemas are strict (additionalProperties false) so a newer-MINOR document fails an older schema copy; the app therefore ignores unknown fields and hides features missing at a lower MINOR instead of validating against the bundled schema.

nodes.label: IV as a forecast of RV: biased but informative
nodes.norm_label: iv as a forecast of rv: biased but informative
nodes.rationale: b != 1 in the RV on IV regression because of the premium and, under long memory, fractional cointegration makes OLS slopes biased downward; squared daily returns are a noisy yardstick.

nodes.label: Multi-step GARCH variance forecast G_t(a)
nodes.rationale: G_t(a) is a real-world (P) annualised variance for the 21 sessions after t+a. The rv21 track compares G_t(0) with realised variance; the vix_level track compares 100*sqrt(G_t(h)) with VIX_{t+h}, whose window it matches.

nodes.label: Variance risk premium (implied versus realised volatility)
nodes.norm_label: variance risk premium (implied versus realised volatility)
nodes.rationale: The two standard definitions have opposite signs (Carr and Wu: realised minus swap rate is negative on average; Bollerslev, Tauchen and Zhou: IV^2 minus RV). The premium makes IV exceed expected RV, so raw GARCH is predicted to sit below VIX on average.

nodes.label: VIX computation and meaning (model-free variance strip)
nodes.norm_label: vix computation and meaning (model-free variance strip)
nodes.rationale: (VIX/100)^2 is an annualised risk-neutral (Q) expected variance over the next 30 calendar days, not a real-world forecast of realised volatility. The 2003 redefinition replaced OEX at-the-money IV with an SPX out-of-the-money strip weighted by 1/K^2, following variance-swap replication theory.

nodes.label: Calibrated *_cal models (v_hat = a_h + b_h G_t(h) by OLS)
nodes.norm_label: calibrated *_cal models (v_hat = a_h + b_h g_t(h) by ols)
nodes.rationale: The gap they absorb equals a_h only if b_h=1, and equals the average VRP only if G is unbiased.

nodes.label: From a GARCH forecast to vol points (summed conditional variances)
nodes.norm_label: from a garch forecast to vol points (summed conditional variances)
nodes.rationale: Conditional variances are summed, not 21*sigma^2_{t+1|t}, because variance mean-reverts; worked example gives 22.61 vol points against a naive 23.81. arch 8.0.0 analytic path matched the recursion to 2.2e-16.

nodes.label: Why VIX squared is approximately a variance-swap rate
nodes.norm_label: why vix squared is approximately a variance-swap rate
nodes.rationale: Ito calculus plus a Taylor expansion write the log payoff as a forward plus a 1/K^2 option strip. Approximate because strikes are discrete and truncated, two expiries are interpolated, and with jumps the strip prices 2(e^J-1-J) rather than J^2 (for J=-0.1: 0.009675 vs 0.010000), so crash jumps put VIX^2 slightly below a true variance-swap rate.

nodes.label: What VIX is: Cboe formula with minutes/525,600 and 30-day interpolation
nodes.norm_label: what vix is: cboe formula with minutes/525,600 and 30-day interpolation
nodes.rationale: The bracket is the risk-neutral variance of the next 30 calendar days; N365/N30 puts it per calendar year. Cboe's Appendix 3 inputs reproduce 13.93 (13.9278 here).

nodes.label: H2: implied variance exceeds later realised variance (VRP), so raw GARCH sits below the future VIX
nodes.norm_label: h2: implied variance exceeds later realised variance (vrp), so raw garch sits below the future vix

nodes.label: VRP and the P-versus-Q gap between GARCH and VIX
nodes.norm_label: vrp and the p-versus-q gap between garch and vix
nodes.rationale: (VIX/100)^2 - G = VRP + (E^P[v] - G): a perfect GARCH still misses VIX by the VRP, and a difference of variances is not a difference of vols (2.39 vs 10.66 vol points). Hence ADR-0001 keeps a P-vs-P track (GARCH vs RV21) beside the P-vs-Q track (GARCH vs VIX).

Patton's MAE-prop divides by the forecast and is not the project's MAPE (measured minimiser 2.36 sigma^2, rewarding over-forecasts).

nodes.rationale: GJR's own eq. 9 puts the indicator on positive shocks; reparameterising (alpha=g1+g2, gamma=-g2) gives the modern negative-shock form with identical economics. Whether asymmetric models beat GARCH(1,1) on SPX is an M3 hypothesis (Hansen and Lunde 2005 found mixed evidence).

nodes.label: Why GARCH on the IV level is a category error
nodes.norm_label: why garch on the iv level is a category error
nodes.rationale: Setting r_t := VIX_t breaks GARCH three ways: wrong mean equation (persistent level makes eps^2 autocorrelated, absorbed into alpha+beta), wrong object (sigma^2 becomes vol-of-vol in VIX points squared), wrong units. Legitimate uses are GARCH-family on SPX returns and ARIMA-GARCH on dlog VIX.

nodes.label: GARCH on the VIX level is a category error (measured)
nodes.norm_label: garch on the vix level is a category error (measured)
nodes.rationale: VIX is already a persistent conditional-volatility forecast, so eps=V-mu violates E[eps]=0 and mean dynamics are mislabelled as clustering. Simulated homoskedastic AR(1) with constant mean gives alpha 0.923-0.976 and alpha+beta 0.946-0.976 (spurious ARCH); with an AR(1) mean alpha is 0-0.0315 and implied variance 0.983-1.029 against the true 1.

nodes.label: GARCH fitted on S&P 500 returns, not the VIX level
nodes.norm_label: garch fitted on s&p 500 returns, not the vix level
nodes.rationale: GARCH models the changing variance of a return series; fitted to the VIX level it would model the variance of the VIX, not the VIX. GARCH, GJR and EGARCH are fitted to daily returns and converted to an annualised 21-session variance forecast, compared like with like against rv21 and against the future VIX (gap = H2).
